## Reflection

The call was driven by two independent wells at 0.3 and 3 uM showing essentially identical massive tubulin signals (tub_std z +74.7 to +75.1, tub_mean +42.8 to +46.0, tub_GLCM contrast +59.6 to +65.5) with microscopist bundling and lower density, plus atlas ranking to Microtubule stabilizers at 0.94-0.96 similarity, which together correctly distinguished increased bundled polymer from destabilizer loss as described for paclitaxel in PMID 25213191 and PMID 31029218.

The main distractors were Eg5 inhibitors (3/10) and Protein degradation (2/10) atlas neighbours, which share mitotic arrest and multinucleation but cannot explain the magnitude and interphase pattern of tubulin increase; ChEMBL Tubulin inhibitor on unblinding was directionally ambiguous, and tubulin-degradation literature in PMID 37356337 helped separate loss-of-mass from stabilization.

I left discrimination on the table by not acquiring a low-dose threshold well to define onset EC50 and by not testing washout reversibility or spindle polarity, which would have more cleanly excluded Eg5 monopolarity during the blinded phase.

What was right:
- Massive tubulin intensity and texture increase replicated across 0.3 uM and 3 uM correctly pointed to stabilization, not microtubule loss.
- Visual bundled rings/cages with lower density matched stabilizer morphology over destabilizer diffuse loss.
- Atlas top matches to Microtubule stabilizers (5/10 at 0.94-0.96 similarity) correctly outranked Eg5 and Protein degradation mimics.

What was wrong or missed:
- Eg5 inhibitor and Protein degradation atlas hits reflecting shared mitotic/multinucleate features were not further excluded by monopolar vs bundled-spindle imaging during blinded phase.
- ChEMBL Tubulin inhibitor label does not distinguish stabilizer vs destabilizer, so unblinding alone could not validate directionality without imaging data.
- No low-dose or washout well was acquired, so onset EC50 and reversibility of bundling were left undefined.

Proposed next experiment: In vitro tubulin polymerization dose-response plus phospho-histone H3 mitotic index and washout imaging to confirm increased polymer mass with bundled microtubules and reversibility versus Eg5 monopolar spindles.
